svg.title: Vault UI Design for Android, iOS, and macOS
svg.desc: Mobile and macOS screens, connection states, appearance, and interaction guidance.

g.text: VAULT / ANDROID + iOS + macOS UI SYSTEM 01
Connection, profiles, diagnostics, and app information across platforms.
Review the profile and tap Connect.
Choose a profile for your next connection.
Server, DNS, and MTU edits apply
Test VPN DNS, TCP, HTTPS, and app access.
Select log text to copy troubleshooting details.
Basic info · Server · DNS and MTU
See the specification for native navigation and safe areas
Vault Android + iOS + macOS · UI specification
Mobile cards share a structure at the default text size and grow for larger text. Icons and text indicate state.
No server configuration has been added.
Use “Add Profile” as the primary action.
Hide addresses, elapsed time, and traffic.
Keep the status and primary action clear.
Show indeterminate progress and block repeat taps.
Keep feedback visible during the permission flow.
Keep the status and primary action clear.
Show Connected and start the timer when the tunnel is ready.
Keep the center button size and switch its action to Disconnect.
Show addresses and live traffic on one screen at default text size.
Show addresses and traffic once the tunnel recovers.
Keep the status and primary action clear.
Keep status feedback visible until the tunnel closes.
Return to Disconnected when the tunnel closes.
Keep the status and primary action clear.
Could not resolve the server address
Reuse the disconnected layout with a failure title and rose retry icon.
Use the round retry icon to retry the connection on all platforms.
Show one readable reason and keep profile switching and diagnostics available.
Show the first connection timeout and retain the reason after cleanup.
Clear the previous failure reason when a new connection starts.
System permission is required to connect
Reuse the failure layout with an amber outline shield.
Offer an action to request authorization again.
Keep the action visible if the user dismisses the permission prompt.
Keep the status and primary action clear.
System permission is required to connect
Explain validation errors and disabled actions. Protect the running profile from accidental changes.
Enter an IP address or hostname without a URL scheme.
Place errors next to their fields and make them available to screen readers.
Pause editing while the save completes.
Return to the profile list and tell the user when changes apply.
Disconnect before renaming or deleting the profile.
Other fields follow the normal editing rules.
Could not read or save the password
Keep the current draft to prevent data loss.
Check system credential storage and try again.
Keep errors visible in the form.
Prioritize diagnostic results and progress. Give logs clear empty, loading, and action states.
Run direct checks while disconnected. Connect to check the full tunnel.
Direct checks and runtime logs are available
Some checks failed or did not complete.
Make route and error details selectable.
Show brief feedback and keep the logs as they are.
Direct and tunnel checks use the same flow. Cancellation stops the current run and retains completed results.
Progress continues until the user taps Cancel checks.
On Android, show a brief pending state if the worker is still stopping.
Show immediately on Apple platforms. Keep completed results.
Use semantic colors to distinguish states, preserve contrast, and separate card surfaces.
Review the profile and tap Connect.
Android uses values-night. iOS and macOS use dynamic colors.
Share design tokens and information hierarchy. Follow each platform’s interaction conventions.
Body text 14–16sp on Android and 17pt on iOS
Technical text and logs start at 12. Use a monospaced font for technical values.
Secondary text #526078 in light mode and #A7B0C2 in dark mode
Reserve #8A96A8 for disabled or decorative elements.
20-unit card radius and 24-unit connection card radius
Hide the Android bottom bar and scroll to the active field when the keyboard opens.
Wrap or expand long hostnames and IPv6 addresses.
Allow selection of addresses and log text.
Test compact and wide layouts and larger text.
Reflow content when text needs more room.
Keep action areas intact when content scrolls.
Android uses a compact Material bar with scalable labels.
iOS uses TabView and Dynamic Type.
macOS uses native windows and visible keyboard focus.
Support safe areas, the Back gesture, and keyboard access.
Give the connection button pressed and disabled states.
Confirm destructive actions such as clearing and deleting.
Respect Reduce Motion during state transitions.
Use one outline per status icon. Highlight selected controls with an accent surface.
Native interactions and shared visual design
Show WAN, IPv4, and IPv6 when available.
Use tabular numerals for traffic and elapsed time.
Hide address cards when no addresses are available.
Show the latest latency after a reply arrives.
Show — while measuring and hide unavailable values.
Format units and decimals for the locale.
Test Chinese, English, Japanese, Korean, and text expansion.
The top badge shows service status and can be hidden where appropriate.
Show latency only when there is a measurement.
01 Tokens and components → 02 Connection states → 03 Profiles and validation → 04 Diagnostics and logs → 05 Appearance, localization, and accessibility
Verify VPN permissions, reconnect and disconnect, profile switching, DNS validation, diagnostic expansion, log actions, both appearances, and larger text.
Keep frequent connection actions in the menu bar. Use native windows for settings, diagnostics, and logs.
Set up an encrypted tunnel to your private network
Keep the app name, connection status, and profile visible.
Hide unavailable network data while disconnected.
Use the power icon to connect and the retry icon to try again.
Settings, Diagnostics, and Quit use an icon and label.
Express status through icon, text, and color.
Show elapsed time, tunnel addresses, and live rates together.
Keep routine checks available from the menu bar.
Use tabular numerals for time and traffic.
Allow users to reveal long addresses.
Show addresses and traffic again once the tunnel recovers.
Selecting the central control disconnects the tunnel.
Hide addresses, elapsed time, and traffic once disconnected.
Each window shows the default 800 × 620 pt content area and the native title bar. The sidebar is 150 pt wide.
Closing a window keeps the VPN running. Quit ends the connection.
Leave empty for defaults. Only assigned tunnel families are used.
Assigned by the server. Addresses may change after reconnecting.
A secure VPN client for cross-regional connectivity.

Show diagnostic results prominently. Logs support source filters, search, auto-scroll, and copy.
Enter comma-separated probe domains. Leave blank to use defaults.
